<reason>A razor-thin but real edge to PRO. This was an unusually even, high-quality exchange. CON's sharpest weapons were the baseline/relaunch adjudication problem, the "backward-looking grievance vs. forward-looking decision aid" distinction, and the claim that the flag steers shoppers to worse purchases when the shrunk brand is still cheapest per gram. PRO blunted these reasonably: the mechanical SKU-history baseline plus the "evasion has never been a reason to legalize evasion" analogy reduced the implementation attack to ordinary consumer-law furniture, and the "resentment is the market's sanction" reframe gave a dynamic-incentive answer to the distortion charge that CON never fully dismantled. Crucially, PRO's inattention dilemma (if shoppers ignore labels, your own 'enforce unit-price rules' fix dies too) was the single most decisive moment, and CON's escape — attention is scarce, not zero; consolidate one number — was coherent but strained, since a flag is at least as salient as a unit price. CON also quietly reframed the motion as a pure "flag mandate," while the proposition as written includes clearer unit-price display, which CON's own fix effectively endorses; PRO under-exploited this but still fought on the motion as written. CON kept one unresolved point (the arithmetic making symmetric orange-sticker shelves inevitable was never squarely answered), which keeps the margin narrow. Both sides complied with Q/A format, both suffered equal clipping costs, and both closed by crystallizing rather than dumping new material. On the whole, PRO made the deciding question — should a hidden price increase be made visible — cleaner and answered the most important pressure more honestly.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Pressure Q1 ("if inattention makes my flag useless, why doesn't it make your enforcement equally useless?") followed by the B4.5 dilemma forced CON into the "scarce, not zero attention; consolidate one number" defense — the pivotal exchange of the debate, and CON's answer was the weakest link in an otherwise strong case.</best_rebuttal>
